### What would you like to be added?

As discussed, the etcd Auth feature continues to receive regular security vulnerability reports which indicate that the feature was never really finished and should not have been graduated to general availability.  This issue proposes that Auth (and RBAC) be reverted to official Beta status so that our users know how much they can currently trust it, and to broaden the contributor pool to work on completing RBAC coverage and returning it to GA status.

As such, I propose to do the following on approval:

- [ ] announce the beta status to our community, including possibly a blog post
- [ ] mark the feature as beta in all documentation pages for supported versions which cover Auth and RBAC
- [ ] publish a set of required changes for returning the feature to GA (see below)
- [ ] convert all security reports related to Auth/RBAC to regular bug issues
- [ ] update our security report policy to indicate this status

Here are my suggested draft requirements for returning Auth/RBAC to GA:

- [ ] closure of all known existing security vulnerabilities reported against Auth/RBAC
- [ ] addition of contributors who work on Auth/RBAC to the SRC
- [ ] a month with no more than one new, verified vulnerability reported against the feature
- [ ] an audit to verify that RBAC covers all etcd operations to which it would be expected to apply
- [ ] addition of reasonably complete test coverage (unit and E2E) to verify Auth/RBAC security and functionality

Please discuss and revise so that we can do an official announcement and start moving on this.  Thanks!

body_text:
What happened?

store.hash reads s.b without holding s.mu (server/storage/mvcc/kvstore.go:160), while store.Restore replaces s.b under
s.mu.Lock (kvstore.go:299). Restore runs when a member applies a snapshot (EtcdServer.applySnapshot), and hash runs for the
Maintenance.Hash RPC through HashStorage.Hash, so the two can run at the same time. hash also reads s.currentRev without
revMu (kvstore.go:164), the read the TODO in that function refers to; Restore writes it at kvstore.go:305.

Running Hash concurrently with Restore under the race detector reports:

```
WARNING: DATA RACE
Write at 0x00c0002bb7d8 by goroutine 74:
  go.etcd.io/etcd/server/v3/storage/mvcc.(*store).Restore()
      server/storage/mvcc/kvstore.go:299
Previous read at 0x00c0002bb7d8 by goroutine 83:
  go.etcd.io/etcd/server/v3/storage/mvcc.(*store).hash()
      server/storage/mvcc/kvstore.go:160
  go.etcd.io/etcd/server/v3/storage/mvcc.(*hashStorage).Hash()
      server/storage/mvcc/hash.go:136
```

What did you expect to happen?

hash synchronizes with Restore on s.mu, as hashByRev and the txn paths do, and the race detector reports nothing.

How can we reproduce it?

Add this test to server/storage/mvcc/kvstore_test.go and run `go test -race -run '^TestHashConcurrentWithRestore$'
./storage/mvcc/` from server/. On main (b25719d10) it failed in 40 of 40 runs.

```go
// TestHashConcurrentWithRestore ensures that Hash does not race with Restore
// replacing the backend. The race detector reports a failure if it does.
func TestHashConcurrentWithRestore(t *testing.T) {
	b, _ := betesting.NewDefaultTmpBackend(t)
	s := NewStore(zaptest.NewLogger(t), b, &lease.FakeLessor{}, StoreConfig{})
	s.Put([]byte("foo"), []byte("bar"), lease.NoLease)

	newBackend, _ := betesting.NewDefaultTmpBackend(t)
	s2 := NewStore(zaptest.NewLogger(t), newBackend, &lease.FakeLessor{}, StoreConfig{})
	s2.Put([]byte("foo"), []byte("bar2"), lease.NoLease)
	s2.Close()

	var wg sync.WaitGroup
	wg.Add(1)
	go func() {
		defer wg.Done()
		if _, _, err := s.HashStorage().Hash(); err != nil {
			t.Error(err)
		}
	}()
	err := s.Restore(newBackend)
	wg.Wait()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}

	cleanup(s, newBackend)
	b.Close()
}
```

Anything else we need to know?

The impact looks limited. HashStorage.Hash and the Hash RPC are documented as intended for testing, and usually the call
just hashes either the old or the new backend. I have not seen a crash or a wrong result on a running server; the race was
found with a unit test. One related window: if hash reads the old s.b and is then delayed until applySnapshot has finished
Restore and closed the old backend, its ForceCommit runs on the closed backend, and with the server's pre-commit hook that
panics in bbolt (checked in isolation, not observed end to end). HashKV (hashByRev) already takes s.mu.RLock and is not
affected.

Etcd version: main at b25719d10 and v3.7.2 (68c065e56), both reproduced with the test above (go1.27.2 and go1.26.8,
linux/amd64). The same code is in v3.6.15. Configuration: none, unit test only.

      	Test:       	TestForceNewCluster_AddLearner_MemberCount/create_a_snapshot_after_adding_learner

### Github Action / Prow Job link

https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-etcd-e2e-arm64/2109510544401633280

### Reason for failure (if possible)

All of these tests have the same error
`fork/exec /home/prow/go/src/github.com/etcd-io/etcd/bin/etcdctl: operation not permitted`

I am fairly certain that the error comes from the `creack/pty` package that is used when calling etcdctl
https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/blob/0155117751ed44874dc64d688c45eeb26c7d0e07/pkg/expect/expect.go#L80

It looks like this error has been encountered by others before and their solution was to downgrade `creack/pty` to `v1.1.19`
https://dev.to/a1ex/buildkite-agent-bug-forkexec-operation-not-permitted-2d08
https://github.com/buildkite/agent/pull/2791

I looked through previous CI failures (links below) and I could not find this error appearing before August 18th and coincidentally creack/pty version was also bumped from `v1.1.18 -> v1.1.24` on August 18th.
https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/pull/22272

A comment in the `creack/pty` repo claims the issue has been fixed in the main branch, but I see that the fix has not been included in a new release yet.
https://github.com/creack/pty/issues/196#issuecomment-5578172067

Downgrading `creack/pty` to `v1.1.18` or `v1.1.19` could potentially be short term fix.

### Anything else we need to know?

Every prow job I found that seems to have failed because of
`fork/exec /home/prow/go/src/github.com/etcd-io/etcd/bin/etcdctl: operation not permitted`

These are roughly in order from latest to earliest date. A lot of these are just the same tests failing for the same reason

### Bug report criteria

- [x] This bug report is not security related, security issues should be disclosed privately via [the report form](https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/security/advisories/new).
- [x] This is not a support request or question, support requests or questions should be raised in the etcd [discussion forums](https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/discussions).
- [x] You have read the etcd [bug reporting guidelines](https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/blob/main/Documentation/contributor-guide/reporting_bugs.md).
- [x] Existing open issues along with etcd [frequently asked questions](https://etcd.io/docs/latest/faq) have been checked and this is not a duplicate.

### What happened?

With `m2` and `m2b` on one session, and `m1` and `m3` on two others, all on one prefix:

1. `m1` locks.
2. `m2.Lock` starts and waits for `m1`.
3. While `m2.Lock` waits, `m2b.TryLock` fails with `mutex: Locked by another session`.
4. `m3.Lock` starts and waits for `m1`; then `m2b.Lock` starts and waits.
5. After `m1.Unlock`, `m3.Lock` returns nil, then `m2.Lock` too, while `m3` holds the lock.

The test below runs these steps (output trimmed):

```
--- FAIL: TestMutexLockKeyRecreated (0.10s)
        	Error:      	An error is expected but got nil.
        	Messages:   	m2 locked while m3 holds the lock
```

The same happens whenever another `Mutex` on the session and prefix of a waiting `Lock` deletes the session's key (a failed `TryLock` or a canceled `Lock`) and a `Lock` on that session recreates the key after another session's key.


### What did you expect to happen?

`m2.Lock` should not return nil while `m3` holds the lock.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Integration test: [`TestMutexLockKeyRecreated`](https://github.com/upamanyus/etcd/blob/fix/mutex-lock-recreated/tests/integration/clientv3/concurrency/mutex_test.go#L64-L115) on branch [`upamanyus/etcd:fix/mutex-lock-recreated`](https://github.com/upamanyus/etcd/tree/fix/mutex-lock-recreated), off `main` (22cc5d9ac). On `main` it fails as above.

### Anything else we need to know?

### Bug report criteria

- [x] This bug report is not security related, security issues should be disclosed privately via [the report form](https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/security/advisories/new).
- [x] This is not a support request or question, support requests or questions should be raised in the etcd [discussion forums](https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/discussions).
- [x] You have read the etcd [bug reporting guidelines](https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/blob/main/Documentation/contributor-guide/reporting_bugs.md).
- [x] Existing open issues along with etcd [frequently asked questions](https://etcd.io/docs/latest/faq) have been checked and this is not a duplicate.

### What happened?

After a supported one-minor-at-a-time upgrade v3.5.34 → v3.6.15 → v3.7.2, the v3.7.2 member panics on startup and crash-loops:

```
{"level":"panic","caller":"schedule/schedule.go:202","msg":"execute job failed","job":"server_applyAll","panic":"unmarshal should never fail (proto: cannot parse invalid wire-format data)"}
```

The WAL replay hits entries that a v3.5 member wrote: v3.5 publishes its member attributes and the cluster version as v2 `pb.Request` entries (`PUT /0/members/<id>/attributes`, `PUT /0/version`) on every start. v3.6 still decodes them (`server/etcdserver/server.go` v3.6.15, `applyEntryNormal`: `MaybeUnmarshal` into `InternalRaftRequest`, fallback to `pb.Request` + `v2ToV3Request`). In v3.7.2, `server/etcdserver/apply/apply.go` `Apply` calls `pbutil.MustUnmarshalMessage(&raftReq, e.Data)` without that fallback, and before the `shouldApplyV3` / consistent-index check, so it panics even on entries that are already applied to the backend.

It happens whenever such an entry is still after the member's last WAL snapshot. v3.6 takes a WAL snapshot every 10000 entries (`--snapshot-count` default), so any cluster that is upgraded to 3.7 within 10000 raft entries after its last v3.5 member restarted is affected. On a 3-member cluster we hit it on the first member rolled to v3.7.2; a single member reproduces it as well (below).

`etcdutl check v2store` (v3.5.34) reported `No custom content found in both v2store and WAL records` on the same data dirs before the upgrade, so the pre-upgrade check does not catch it. The [3.6 → 3.7 upgrade guide](https://etcd.io/docs/v3.7/upgrades/upgrade_3_7/) requires 3.6.11+, which is met (3.6.15).

### What did you expect to happen?

v3.7.2 starts on a data dir last used by a healthy v3.6.15 member, as the rolling upgrade guide describes. Or, if this is intentionally unsupported, the 3.6 → 3.7 guide (and ideally `etcdutl check v2store` or a startup check with a clear error) states that legacy v2 entries must be past the last WAL snapshot before the upgrade.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Single member, same data dir, Docker:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Minimal reproduction: single member, same data dir, 3.5.34 -> 3.6.15 -> 3.7.2.
set -euo pipefail
VOL=etcd-repro-data
docker rm -f etcd-repro >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
docker volume rm $VOL >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
docker volume create $VOL >/dev/null

run() {  # $1 = image tag
  docker run -d --name etcd-repro -v $VOL:/data gcr.io/etcd-development/etcd:$1 \
    /usr/local/bin/etcd --name n1 --data-dir /data \
    --listen-client-urls http://0.0.0.0:2379 --advertise-client-urls http://127.0.0.1:2379 \
    --listen-peer-urls http://0.0.0.0:2380 --initial-advertise-peer-urls http://127.0.0.1:2380 \
    --initial-cluster n1=http://127.0.0.1:2380 --initial-cluster-state new >/dev/null
  for _ in $(seq 30); do docker exec etcd-repro etcdctl endpoint health >/dev/null 2>&1 && return 0; sleep 1; done
  echo "$1: not healthy"; docker logs etcd-repro 2>&1 | grep -E '"level":"(panic|fatal)"' | head -3; return 1
}
stop() { docker stop -t 10 etcd-repro >/dev/null; docker rm etcd-repro >/dev/null; }

for tag in v3.5.34 v3.6.15; do
  run $tag
  for i in $(seq 100); do docker exec etcd-repro etcdctl put /k$i v >/dev/null; done
  echo "$tag: $(docker exec etcd-repro etcdctl endpoint status -w json | jq -c '.[0].Status | {version, raftIndex}')"
  stop
done
run v3.7.2 && echo "v3.7.2: started OK"
```

Output:

```
v3.5.34: {"version":"3.5.34","raftIndex":105}
v3.6.15: {"version":"3.6.15","raftIndex":209}
v3.7.2: not healthy
{"level":"panic",...,"msg":"execute job failed","job":"server_applyAll","panic":"unmarshal should never fail (proto: cannot parse invalid wire-format data)",...}
```

Workaround (verified with the same script): on v3.6.15 write more than `--snapshot-count` (10000) entries before switching the binary, e.g. `etcdctl check perf --load=s` twice (raft index 18214). v3.7.2 then starts fine, because WAL replay begins after the new snapshot.

### Anything else we need to know?

- Found while rehearsing a production upgrade of a 3-member TLS cluster (official images, Kubernetes StatefulSet). Decoding that cluster's WAL with the v3.7.2 `etcdserverpb` showed 37 undecodable normal entries, all v2 requests for `/0/members/<id>/attributes` and `/0/version`, written by v3.5.x members at start (3.6 members write none). The crash happened on the first entry after the last `.snap`.
- While at least one member is still on 3.6, rolling the crashed member back to v3.6.15 recovers it.
- Possible fixes: keep the v2 `pb.Request` decode fallback in v3.7 (or treat those entries as no-ops), or skip decoding entries with index ≤ consistent index; and/or document the requirement in the upgrade guide and detect it in `etcdutl check v2store`.

```console
$ etcd --version
etcd Version: 3.7.2
Git SHA: 68c065e
Go Version: go1.26.8
Go OS/Arch: linux/arm64
```

Previous versions on the same data dir: v3.5.34, then v3.6.15 (official images `gcr.io/etcd-development/etcd`).

### Etcd configuration (command line flags or environment variables)

Minimal repro: only the flags in the script above. Production-like cluster: 3 members, client mTLS, `--peer-auto-tls`, `--auto-compaction-mode=periodic --auto-compaction-retention=72h`, default `--snapshot-count`.

The v3.7.2 member does not start. Last status on v3.6.15 before switching:

```
{"version":"3.6.15","raftIndex":209}
```

### What would you like to be added?

A per-member self-check loop on the server, reported through the grpc.health.v1 service etcd already registers, plus an opt-in clientv3 dial option that drops a NOT_SERVING member from the client's endpoint rotation.

Prior art: grpc.health.v1 has been registered since v3.3 (#8121). #16278 made the aggregate entry flip to NOT_SERVING during defrag, behind `StopGRPCServiceOnDefrag` (planned for deprecation in 3.8 and removal in 3.9, per the discussion in #18882). The client half has been proposed twice and closed unmerged: #18882 (health check in the default service config) and #21674 (opt-in dial option); #16276, the original request, was closed stale. #18882 closed on the argument that non-blocking defragmentation (#22425) removes the main motivation, leaving open which scenarios beyond defrag remain. The list below is those scenarios.

#### Proposal

Server side, gated behind a new `ServerHealthCheck` feature gate (Alpha, default off): the loop probes the serving path on a fixed interval and reports each dimension as its own grpc.health.v1 entry.

| Entry | Healthy when |
| --- | --- |
| `etcd.health/linear_read` | a linearizable read probe completes within the request-timeout budget |
| `etcd.health/serializable_read` | a serializable read probe completes (the local read path) |
| `etcd.health/apply_lag` | committed − applied stays below a threshold |
| `etcd.health/apply_stall` | applied keeps advancing while committed advances |
| `etcd.health/no_leader` | the member has a leader |
| `etcd.health/data_corruption` | no CORRUPT alarm names this member |
| `etcd.health/learner` | the member is not a learner |
| `etcd.health/defrag` | no Defragment is running (reference-counted across concurrent RPCs) |

The aggregate entry (service name `""`, the health.v1 overall-server convention) is what clients watch. Only member-local conditions flip it to NOT_SERVING: `linear_read` failing after a bounded `no_leader` veto expires, `apply_stall`, a CORRUPT alarm naming this member, `learner`, and `defrag`. `no_leader` and `apply_lag` stay on their own entries, because they hold on every member at the same time: either would evict every endpoint during one election and turn a single `ErrNoLeader` into a retry storm. NOSPACE does not participate for the same reason: it trips on all members at once while reads still work.

Keeping `serializable_read` next to `linear_read` preserves attribution: during a lost-quorum window the local read path stays green, so a failing `linear_read` with a passing `serializable_read` distinguishes a broken local path from a missing consensus path. The `no_leader` veto on `linear_read` is bounded at `max(30s, 10 × election timeout)`: within the window an election is assumed in progress; past it the member is presumed stranded and is evicted. The defrag entry is driven by Defragment execution itself, so it covers what #16278 wired behind `StopGRPCServiceOnDefrag` without that gate. A client that needs "the cluster currently has no leader" watches `etcd.health/no_leader` or observes `ErrNoLeader` on linearizable operations; the aggregate is member-scoped.

Client side, opt-in dial options, following #21674:

```go
cli, err := clientv3.New(clientv3.Config{
	Endpoints:   []string{"member-0", "member-1", "member-2"},
	DialOptions: healthcheck.GRPCClientHealthCheckOptions(),
})
```

The helper also disables the resolver's service config, because clientv3's manual resolver always publishes one, which would otherwise take precedence over `healthCheckConfig`; the same round_robin policy is written back, so default endpoint selection is unchanged.

Enabling the server gate reroutes nothing on its own: health.v1 is passive reporting, and only clients passing the dial options change behavior. State transitions are debounced (consecutive failure/success thresholds), and the `etcd_server_healthcheck_*` metrics expose state, last tick, transitions, per-check latency and failure counts, suppressed ticks, apply lag, learner flag, and checker anomalies.

Defaults: 500ms interval, per-check timeout derived from the request-timeout budget (the same budget a linearizable read gets), failure/success thresholds 3/2. Tunables: `--experimental-health-check-{interval,timeout,apply-lag,failure-threshold,success-threshold}`.

#### Non-goals

- `/livez` and `/readyz` are unchanged.
- No cross-member negotiation: each member evaluates only its own serving path.
- No default-on. Whether the client opt-in should become the default service config (the original #18882 ask) is worth revisiting once the server side has a track record; this proposal keeps it opt-in.
- `monitorLeader` / interceptor integration for the watch-staleness case in #13527 is out of scope; the per-check entries give it a natural consumer later.

#### Open questions

1. Aggregate eligibility: member-local conditions only, as above. Is that the right rule?
2. Naming: is `etcd.health/<check>` the right scheme, and should the aggregate live at service name `""`, or should a named aggregate entry also exist?
3. Check set: anything missing, anything that should not be there?
4. Flag surface: one feature gate plus five `--experimental-health-check-*` tunables, or fewer knobs?

#### Implementation status

A working implementation exists: server loop, health.v1 wiring, client opt-in, metrics, and unit, integration, and e2e chaos tests covering leader loss, partitions, stalled apply, corruption alarms, defrag, goroutine leaks, and shutdown. I plan to submit it against `main` once the direction is agreed.

### Why is this needed?

All of the failures below have the same property: the member process is up, its gRPC connection stays Ready, and the member cannot usefully serve. Nothing at the connection layer tells the client to move.

1. Stalled apply loop. raft keeps committing while applied freezes. Linearizable reads time out waiting for the read index to apply, but the connection stays Ready, so clients keep the endpoint and pay the timeout on every consensus operation.
2. A CORRUPT alarm naming one member. The remedy is to send reads to the other members, but a gRPC client has no in-band way to know; only an external prober reading `/readyz` can act on it.
3. A partitioned member with stalled disk I/O that never steps down. Its watches are not cancelled and keep serving stale data (#13527).
4. A learner in the client's endpoint list, with no signal that it is a non-voting member (#18801).
5. Defrag, narrowed but not gone. Non-blocking defragmentation (#22425) shortens the blocking phase to a catch-up window; releases without it still block for the whole copy.

`/livez` and `/readyz` serve external HTTP probers, and an in-process gRPC client cannot consume them. The only in-band statuses a client sees today are the ones the connection layer reports, which stay green through all five cases above.

### Bug report criteria

- [x] This bug report is not security related, security issues should be disclosed privately via [the report form](https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/security/advisories/new).
- [x] This is not a support request or question, support requests or questions should be raised in the etcd [discussion forums](https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/discussions).
- [x] You have read the etcd [bug reporting guidelines](https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/blob/main/Documentation/contributor-guide/reporting_bugs.md).
- [x] Existing open issues along with etcd [frequently asked questions](https://etcd.io/docs/latest/faq) have been checked and this is not a duplicate.

### What happened?

NewTimeoutTransport sets the deprecated `http.Transport.Dial`, but NewTransport has set `DialContext` since v3.5.0 (17b982382), and http.Transport uses `DialContext` when both are set. So rafthttp stream connections have no read or write deadlines. When a peer stops answering without resets, stream readers block until TCP gives up, and the peer stays active in `etcd_network_active_peers` for minutes while the prober already reports it unhealthy.

### What did you expect to happen?

The stream goes inactive after `ConnReadTimeout` (5s), like in v3.4.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Drop traffic between two members of a 3-member cluster with `iptables -I INPUT -s <peer> -j DROP` and `iptables -I OUTPUT -d <peer> -j DROP`. `etcd_network_active_peers` stays 1 and `peer became inactive` isn't logged for minutes.

### Anything else we need to know?

`TestNewTimeoutTransport` calls `tr.Dial` directly, so it doesn't catch this. PR to follow.

### Etcd version (please run commands below)

v3.5.0 and later, including main.

- [x] This bug report is not security related, security issues should be disclosed privately via [the report form](https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/security/advisories/new).
- [x] This is not a support request or question, support requests or questions should be raised in the etcd [discussion forums](https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/discussions).
- [x] You have read the etcd [bug reporting guidelines](https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/blob/main/Documentation/contributor-guide/reporting_bugs.md).
- [x] Existing open issues along with etcd [frequently asked questions](https://etcd.io/docs/latest/faq) have been checked and this is not a duplicate.

### What happened?

NewTimeoutTransport sets the deprecated `http.Transport.Dial`, but NewTransport has set `DialContext` since v3.5.0 (17b982382), and http.Transport uses `DialContext` when both are set. So rafthttp stream connections have no read or write deadlines. When a peer stops answering without resets, stream readers block until TCP gives up, and the peer stays active in `etcd_network_active_peers` for minutes while the prober already reports it unhealthy.

### What did you expect to happen?

The stream goes inactive after `ConnReadTimeout` (5s), like in v3.4.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Drop traffic between two members of a 3-member cluster with `iptables -I INPUT -s <peer> -j DROP` and `iptables -I OUTPUT -d <peer> -j DROP`. `etcd_network_active_peers` stays 1 and `peer became inactive` isn't logged for minutes.

### Anything else we need to know?

`TestNewTimeoutTransport` calls `tr.Dial` directly, so it doesn't catch this. PR to follow.

### Etcd version (please run commands below)

v3.5.0 and later, including main.

### Summary
On Android (OxygenOS 15) using Chrome `145.0.7632.159`, Excalidraw cannot save back to the same `.excalidraw` file after opening it. When invoking **Save to…** again, the original file is shown **greyed out** in the picker and Excalidraw forces choosing a new filename.

This happens even when the file is stored in the **Downloads** directory. On the same device/location, **draw.io** can overwrite the same file, so this looks like an Excalidraw handle/save-flow bug/compat issue.

### Environment
- OS: Android (OxygenOS 15)
- Browser: Chrome `145.0.7632.159`
- Excalidraw version: <!-- fill in from Excalidraw main menu (bottom) -->
- Running as: <!-- browser tab or installed PWA? -->

### Steps to reproduce
1. Open https://excalidraw.com on Android Chrome.
2. Create a drawing.
3. Use **Main menu → Save to…** and save as `test.excalidraw` into **Downloads**.
4. Use **Main menu → Open** and open `test.excalidraw` from **Downloads**.
5. Make any change.
6. Use **Main menu → Save to…** again and navigate to **Downloads**.

### Actual result
- The existing `test.excalidraw` file is **greyed out** in the save picker.
- Excalidraw cannot overwrite it and forces saving under a **new name**.

### Expected result
- After opening an `.excalidraw` file, Excalidraw should retain a writable file handle and allow saving changes back to the **same file** (overwrite), without forcing a new filename.

### Notes / comparison
- Reproducible even in **Downloads** (not only on SD card).
- On the same phone and directory, **draw.io** can overwrite the same filename successfully.
- This suggests Excalidraw may not be obtaining/persisting the `FileSystemFileHandle` on Android Chrome (falls back to “Save as” behavior).

## Key Use Cases
- System Architecture: Showing real-time data flow between microservices.
- User Flows: Highlighting the "happy path" in a UI wireframe.
- Instructional Design: Demonstrating step-by-step processes in live tutorials.

## Technical Implementation
- SVG Animation: Use stroke-dasharray and animate stroke-dashoffset. This is the most performant, native browser method.
- Logic: Normalize animation speed relative to path length to ensure consistent visual flow across different arrow sizes.
- Accessibility: Honor prefers-reduced-motion settings to auto-disable for sensitive users.

## UI Integration
- Toggle: A simple "Animate" checkbox in the arrow property panel.
- Controls: A slider for Speed and a button to Reverse Direction.

When I click the Delete icon on the Excalidraw Text to Diagram page, the diagram is deleted successfully, but the chat title still remains visible on the fresh/empty board.

### Steps to reproduce:

1. Open the Excalidraw Text to Diagram page.
2. Create a diagram using ai.
3. Click the Delete icon.
4. Observe the fresh/empty board.

Actual Result:
The diagram is deleted, but the previous chat title is still visible.

Expected Result:
After deleting the diagram, the fresh board should also clear the previous chat title and show a completely new/empty state.

Recording: The issue is visible in the attached recording.

body_text: ### Issue: The lasso tool is one of the few features in Excalidraw without its own hotkey making quick access difficult. It can currently be selected through the meatballs menu or by clicking on the selection tool twice. You can hold alt while using the selection tool to get a temporary lasso but this doesn't work well for tools that do not allow hold binds. (Holding down the button(s)) ### Use Cases: **1.** Regular keyboard quick access. **2.** Binding the tool to alternate menus as seen on some styli. This is especially useful for styli with few buttons or ones that cannot use hold binds. See the below picture. ### Solution: First mentioned in [#11909](https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw/issues/11909#issuecomment-5616545829). **Create a hot key for the tool.** Suggestions: - **C** (It's next to V for most folks) - **Alt + V** (Similar to "Draw to Shape" as mentioned by @dimateos and does not need to be held throughout use. **Shift + V** would be better but is taken by "Flip Vertical") - **Double tapping V or 1** (This is not as good since a certain stylus may only allow binding 1 key and not a series.)

**Describe the bug**
In the main menu, the canvas background color picker loses its swatch strip and shows only a single enlarged button at tablet-sized viewport widths. On wider viewports it renders the full strip.

The main menu is fixed-width, so viewport size shouldn't affect it.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Open the main menu.
2. Resize the window to a tablet-sized width.
3. Look at the canvas background color picker.

**Expected behavior**
The picker looks the same in the main menu at any viewport width (swatch strip + normal-size trigger).

**Actual behavior**
At tablet-sized widths the swatch strip is hidden and the trigger is enlarged; on wider viewports it is full.

body_text:
Excalidraw's text elements currently support only a single, uniform style (font family, weight, decoration) applied to the entire block. There's no way to make individual words or a range of characters bold or underlined within the same text element.

Current behavior:
Text formatting options apply to the whole text element — no inline/partial formatting is possible.

Expected behavior:
Allow selecting a word or range of text within a text element and applying bold and/or underline just to that selection, similar to standard rich-text editors.

Workaround:
Currently the only way to emphasize part of a sentence is to split it into separate text elements with different styles and manually align them, which is fragile and breaks if the text needs to be edited later.

Related:
This ties into the broader need for per-word/per-character styling (color, bold, underline) within a single text element

When I paste an image into Excalidraw and draw on it with the pen, using the eraser over the drawing also erases parts of the image.

The eraser should only remove the pen drawing and leave the pasted image untouched.

This is quite annoying when using Excalidraw to annotate screenshots/images. It would be great if images could be protected from the eraser.

### Suggested improvement:
Consider making the eraser operate only on erasable drawing elements, or provide a way to lock/protect pasted images from the eraser.

body_text:
A few locale files have placeholder problems that show up at runtime.

### Typo'd placeholder (renders literally)

`chat.errors.promptTooLong`

- en: `Prompt is too long (max {{max}} characters)`
- es-ES: `El mensaje es demasiado largo (máximo {{mix}} caracteres)`

`{{mix}}` doesn't correspond to anything in the source string, so it never
interpolates. Spanish users see the literal text `{{mix}}` in the message.

### Dropped placeholders (value silently lost)

These `si-LK` strings are missing placeholders present in the English source:

- `alerts.confirmAddLibrary` is missing `{{numShapes}}`
- `errors.fileTooBig` is missing `{{maxSize}}`
- `errorSplash.trackedToSentry` is missing `{{eventId}}`

These don't render anything broken, they just lose the number, size, or event
ID the sentence exists to communicate.

### Notes

Found these by running an open-source i18n checker over the locale files.
Since translations are Crowdin-managed, the fixes probably belong there rather
than in a PR against this repo, so flagging here instead of sending a patch.
Happy to open one if you'd prefer the files corrected directly.

Might also be worth a placeholder-parity check in CI between `en.json` and the
translated files. This class of bug is invisible until someone reports a
rendered string.

Following up on #12097 / #12109 — running the same placeholder-parity check
against current `si-LK.json`, I found 5 more instances of the same bug class
that aren't covered by #12109's new test suite (which explicitly documents
si-LK as exempt from the missing-placeholder check).

These are additive to #12097's 3 si-LK findings, not a repeat of them —
different keys entirely.

### Dropped placeholders (value silently lost)

body_text:
### Problem

Excalidraw's scene search works well for text created with the text tool, but handwritten content created using the freehand/drawing tools is not searchable.

As notes become larger and more sketches/diagrams contain handwritten annotations, it becomes difficult to find information that is visually present on the canvas but not represented as searchable text.

### Proposed solution

Extend the existing scene search to also recognize handwritten text and include it in the existing search index.

Ideally, this would work transparently with the current search UI:

Typed text continues to work as it does today.
Handwritten text is recognized locally using a handwriting-text-recognition (HTR) model.
The recognized text is indexed alongside the existing scene text.
Searching for a word found in handwriting returns the corresponding scene/element.
Recognition results can be cached and updated only when the relevant drawing changes.
Client-side / privacy

A client-side implementation would be preferable so that handwriting does not need to be uploaded to a server. A local model could perform the recognition and the generated text could be used only for search indexing.

### Questions

Before implementing this, I'd like to know:

1. Would this functionality be appropriate for Excalidraw's existing scene-search architecture?
2. Is there a preferred client-side OCR/HTR library or model that the project would be open to using?
3. Would maintainers be interested in a PR implementing this functionality?

I'd be happy to work on the implementation if the approach sounds reasonable.

body_text:
### Problem
- The web app currently saves drawings in local browser storage (IndexedDB), which offers no folder organization for managing multiple diagrams.
- Drawings do not sync across devices and risk getting wiped if browser cache is cleared.
- Manually exporting and importing `.excalidraw` files is cumbersome for regular workflows.

### Proposed Solution
Add an optional, client-side Google Drive integration (similar to draw.io):
1. **Connect Drive**: Opt-in "Connect Google Drive" option in the hamburger menu.
2. **Folder Organization**: Use the Google Drive file picker to open and save diagrams into specific Drive folders.
3. **Auto-Save**: Automatically debounce-save canvas edits back to the selected Drive file.

### Why this fits Excalidraw
- **Zero Server Costs**: Uses client-side OAuth (`drive.file` scope) and direct Google Drive API calls—no backend hosting or database required from Excalidraw.
- **Privacy First**: Respects Excalidraw's local-first ethos; files remain in the user's personal Google Drive.

body_text:
`handleCanvasPointerDown`'s logic for temporarily switching to the Eraser
tool while a stylus's hardware eraser button is pressed doesn't check
`state.viewModeEnabled`. Most tools are shielded from this by an earlier
pan.start() check that intercepts pointer-downs in view mode — but tools
meant to stay active in view mode (laser, custom — e.g. a presenter's
laser pointer during a shared view-only session) bypass that check. For
those, a pen's eraser tip can still activate the Eraser tool and actually
erase elements, even though the session is supposed to be read-only.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Load Excalidraw with some elements, with view mode enabled (e.g. a
   shared view-only link) and the "laser" tool active (as a presenter
   would have, via `interaction.enabled.tools.laser`, or by setting it
   programmatically).
2. Touch a stylus's eraser end to an element on the canvas, or from the
   console:

const canvas = document.querySelector('.excalidraw__canvas.interactive');
canvas.dispatchEvent(new PointerEvent('pointerdown', {
  bubbles: true, pointerType: 'pen', button: 5, clientX: 100, clientY: 100,
}));
canvas.dispatchEvent(new PointerEvent('pointerup', {
  bubbles: true, pointerType: 'pen', button: 5, clientX: 100, clientY: 100,
}));

Expected: the laser tool stays active; nothing is erased.
Actual: the active tool silently switches to "Eraser", and the element
at that position gets erased.

**Relevant code**
`packages/excalidraw/components/App.tsx`, `handleCanvasPointerDown`, the
temporary-eraser-switch check — it guards on `isInteractionEnabled()` and
`!props.activeTool`, but not `state.viewModeEnabled`.

### Description

Dropping a sticky note dragged out of the toolbar opens the text editor on the previously selected text instead of on the new note. What you type replaces that text, and the new note is left without a label.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Drag a sticky note out of the toolbar onto the canvas, type `first` and press <kbd>Esc</kbd> (the note stays selected).
2. Drag another sticky note out of the toolbar and drop it elsewhere.
3. Type `second`.

The same happens when a text, a labeled shape or a labeled arrow is the only selected element before the drop.

### Expected

The editor opens on the dropped note, which gets the label `second`. The first note keeps `first`.

### Actual

The editor opens with the first note's text selected. `second` overwrites `first`, and the dropped note has no label.

### Notes

The drop selects the new note with `setState`, which is still pending when `onDrop` starts text editing. `startTextEditing` is called without `textElement`, so it resolves the text to edit from the (old) selection.

body_text:
### Description

When the shape switcher (<kbd>Tab</kbd>) switches a line or arrow back to a type it already had, it puts back the element exactly as it was cached when the switcher first saw it in that type, including its old `version`.

Because the version goes down:

- the switch back isn't recorded in history, and undoing afterwards throws `ElementsDelta invariant broken for element "…"` in development builds, leaving the undo stack empty
- collaborators don't receive the change, since only elements with a higher version are broadcast and reconciled
- anything changed since it was cached (moved, restyled) is reverted

### Steps to reproduce

1. Select a sharp arrow and press <kbd>Tab</kbd> to open the shape switcher.
2. Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> again to switch it to a curved arrow.
3. Nudge it with <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>→</kbd>, or change its stroke color.
4. Press <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>Tab</kbd> to switch it back to a sharp arrow.
5. Press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>/<kbd>Cmd</kbd>+<kbd>Z</kbd>.

### Expected

The arrow is sharp again, keeps the nudge and color, and undo switches it back to curved. Collaborators see the sharp arrow.

### Actual

The nudge and color are lost, undo doesn't bring back the curved arrow (and throws in development), and collaborators keep seeing the curved arrow.

### Notes

`convertElementTypes` reinserts the element from `LINEAR_ELEMENT_CONVERSION_CACHE` as is.

### Description

Opening an earlier save of the current scene (dropping the `.excalidraw` file on the canvas, or <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>/<kbd>Cmd</kbd>+<kbd>O</kbd>) shows the saved content, but the elements it shares with the scene keep their lower, saved `version`. The store only treats an element as changed when its version goes up, so:

- the replace isn't recorded for those elements: undo, as the "Content replaced" toast suggests, doesn't bring back what was there
- later changes to them aren't recorded either, until their version catches up with the one before the load
- in a collaboration session they aren't broadcast, and collaborators keep the newer copies

### Steps to reproduce

1. Draw a rectangle and save the scene to a file.
2. Change the rectangle's stroke color.
3. Drag the saved file onto the canvas. The rectangle gets its original color back.
4. Press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>/<kbd>Cmd</kbd>+<kbd>Z</kbd>: the changed color doesn't come back.
5. Change the rectangle's background color and press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>/<kbd>Cmd</kbd>+<kbd>Z</kbd>: nothing is undone.

### Expected

Undoing the load restores the changed color, and later changes are undoable.

### Actual

Neither the load nor the following change is recorded.

### Notes

Regressed in #10597, which moved bumping the versions of loaded elements above their local copies out of `restoreElements` into `bumpElementVersions`. The app's backend import and collab call it, but `loadSceneOrLibraryFromBlob` (used by file drop and `loadFromJSON`) doesn't.

#10829 is related but about loading a file with different element ids.

body_text:
### Description

Dropping a scene file on the canvas replaces the scene and its image files. History doesn't track files, so undoing the replace (as the "Content replaced" toast suggests) brings back the previous scene's images without their file data. They still show while their bitmaps are cached, but saving, exporting or copying them afterwards produces broken images, and a host persisting `files` from `onChange` loses them.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Add an image to the canvas.
2. Drag any `.excalidraw` file (or a PNG/SVG with an embedded scene) onto the canvas without holding <kbd>Shift</kbd>.
3. Press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>/<kbd>Cmd</kbd>+<kbd>Z</kbd>. The image comes back.
4. Save the scene to a file and open it again.

### Expected

The image is saved with its file and shows up after reopening.

### Actual

The saved file has no data for the image, which shows as broken.

### Notes

Both drop paths pass `replaceFiles: true`, which makes `addMissingFiles` reset the files to the loaded ones. Opening a file with <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>/<kbd>Cmd</kbd>+<kbd>O</kbd> adds to the current files instead, and doesn't have this problem.

### Description

A bucket fill joins the group of the shape it fills, but is created unlocked even when that group is locked. Clicking the fill then selects the whole group, locked elements included, so the locked group can be moved or deleted through it.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Draw two shapes, group them, and lock the group (<kbd>Ctrl</kbd>/<kbd>Cmd</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>L</kbd>).
2. With the bucket fill tool, click inside one of the locked shapes.
3. With the selection tool, drag the fill, or click it and press <kbd>Delete</kbd>.

### Expected

The locked group stays where it is and isn't deleted.

### Actual

The whole locked group moves with the fill, or is deleted.

### Description

While editing a group inside a frame, dragging one of its members within the frame removes it from the group. With two members, the other one is ungrouped too, so the group is gone.

Dragging the same member without a frame keeps the group.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a frame with two shapes inside it, and group the shapes.
2. Double-click one shape to edit the group.
3. Drag that shape a little, keeping it inside the frame.

### Expected

The shapes stay grouped.

### Actual

Both shapes are ungrouped.

### Notes

On pointer up, `handleSelectionDragOnPointerUp` removes every dragged element of the edited group that is in the frame under the pointer from that group. That frame is also the one the element is already in, so elements that don't change frames are removed as well.

body_text:
### Description

Binding a text that has arrows into a container (<kbd>W</kbd> with a text and a container selected, or "Bind text to container" in the context menu) leaves the arrows bound to the text. A label is not bindable, so the arrows no longer follow it, and once the container (and with it the label) is deleted, they keep pointing at the deleted text.

Since #12264, unwrapping a labeled shape that has arrows moves its arrows onto the freed text, so unwrapping a shape and wrapping its text into another one runs into this every time.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Draw a rectangle with a label and an arrow pointing at it.
2. Select the rectangle and press <kbd>W</kbd>. The label is freed, and the arrow now points at it.
3. Select the text and another rectangle, and press <kbd>W</kbd>.
4. Drag that rectangle.

### Expected

The arrow is bound to the rectangle the text was bound to, and follows it.

### Actual

The arrow stays where the text was and doesn't follow the rectangle. Its binding still refers to the text.

The same happens with an arrow-endpoint text (or any text an arrow is bound to). Binding an arrow's endpoint text to that same arrow leaves the arrow bound to its own label.

### Notes

`bindTextToContainer` doesn't move the text's arrows to the container, while `wrapTextsInContainers` and rewrapping an unwrapped container do.

### Description

Saved `.excalidraw` files keep the scene's deleted elements. Inserting such a file into the scene, with <kbd>Shift</kbd>+drop (#12177) or by pasting its contents as text, inserts its deleted elements too:

- the inserted content is centered on the bounds of all the elements, deleted ones included, so the visible part lands away from the pointer, possibly far off-screen
- invisible deleted copies are added to the scene and to the selection

### Steps to reproduce

1. Draw a shape, draw another one far away and delete it, and save the scene to a file.
2. In another scene, hold <kbd>Shift</kbd> and drop the file on the canvas.

### Expected

The visible shape is inserted centered on the pointer, and nothing else is added.

### Actual

The shape is inserted away from the pointer (offset by the deleted shape's position), and a deleted copy of the other shape is added and selected.

### Notes

`addElementsFromPasteOrLibrary` restores the elements it inserts but doesn't leave out the deleted ones. The duplication logs `[NONDELETED][INVARIANT] Element to duplicate should be non-deleted` for them.

### Description

With all of a locked frame's children selected, <kbd>W</kbd> (and "Remove frame" in the context menu) deletes the locked frame.

The locked frame itself can't be selected, but selecting all of a frame's children counts as unwrapping that frame (#12264), and that doesn't check whether the frame is locked.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a frame with a couple of shapes in it, and lock the frame.
2. Select all of its children, e.g. with <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>/<kbd>Cmd</kbd>+<kbd>A</kbd> or a box selection.
3. Press <kbd>W</kbd>, or right-click and pick "Remove frame".

### Expected

The locked frame isn't removed.

### Actual

The locked frame is deleted, and its children are taken out of it.

### Notes

`getFrameToUnwrap` in `actionFrame.ts` doesn't check `frame.locked`.

### Description

Binding a text to a container (<kbd>W</kbd> with a text and a container selected, or "Bind text to container" in the context menu) keeps the text's `frameId` and `groupIds` instead of giving it its container's. The label then belongs to a different frame or group than its container:

- moving the text's old frame moves the label out of its container, which stays put
- a label bound to a container inside a frame isn't one of the frame's children
- selecting a member of the text's old group selects the label without its container

### Steps to reproduce

1. Put a text inside a frame, and draw a rectangle outside the frame.
2. Select both and press <kbd>W</kbd>. The text moves into the rectangle.
3. Select the frame and nudge it with the arrow keys.

### Expected

The label stays in the rectangle.

### Actual

The label moves with the frame, out of the rectangle.

### Notes

`bindTextToContainer` doesn't update the text's `frameId` and `groupIds`. Wrapping a text in a new container gives the container the text's frame and groups, so the two always match there.

### Description

Deleting all of an arrow's points in the line editor deletes the arrow, but leaves its label behind. The label is still drawn, but it can't be selected or deleted, because it's bound to a deleted container. The shapes the arrow was bound to also keep it in their `boundElements`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create an arrow with a label.
2. Open the line editor (<kbd>Ctrl</kbd>/<kbd>Cmd</kbd>+<kbd>Enter</kbd>).
3. Select all of its points (box-select, or <kbd>Shift</kbd>+click) and press <kbd>Delete</kbd>.

### Expected

The arrow and its label are deleted.

### Actual

The arrow is deleted, and its label stays on the canvas, out of reach.

### Notes

The "deleting all points" case of `actionDeleteSelected` only marks the linear element deleted. It doesn't delete its bound text or call `fixBindingsAfterDeletion`, as deleting the selected elements does.

### Description

Deleting an arrow's bound start or end point in the line editor keeps the arrow's binding for that end. The new endpoint isn't on the shape, but the arrow is still bound to it, so it jumps onto the shape the next time the shape (or the arrow) moves.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Draw an arrow with three or more points, ending on a rectangle so that it binds to it.
2. Open the line editor (<kbd>Ctrl</kbd>/<kbd>Cmd</kbd>+<kbd>Enter</kbd>), select the end point, and press <kbd>Delete</kbd>. The arrow now ends in empty space.
3. Move the rectangle.

### Expected

The arrow stays where it is, as it is no longer bound to the rectangle.

### Actual

The arrow's end jumps onto the rectangle and follows it.

The same happens with an arrow-endpoint text: moving the text makes the arrow jump.

### Notes

Deleting points in the line editor (`actionDeleteSelected`, through `LinearElementEditor.deletePoints`) doesn't touch `startBinding` / `endBinding`.

body_text:
### Bug Description
When typing in Excalidraw, there is an unexpected behavior regarding the cursor movement and text alignment based on the language (English vs. Hebrew):
1. **When typing in English:** The cursor moves to the left instead of the right.
2. **When typing in Hebrew:** The letters/text shift to the left incorrectly.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Open Excalidraw (https://excalidraw.com/).
2. Select the Text tool and click on the canvas.
3. Type in English and observe the cursor direction.
4. Type in Hebrew and observe how the letters behave.

### Expected Behavior
- When typing in English (LTR), the cursor should naturally move to the right.
- When typing in Hebrew (RTL), text input and cursor behavior should follow standard RTL conventions correctly.

body_text:
**What happens**

Pasting a Giphy page link such as

```
https://giphy.com/gifs/theoffice-the-office-tv-michael-scott-ZK2W0gl0w0vkI
```

creates a web embed for `https://giphy.com/embed/theoffice`. The id is taken from the first word of the slug instead of the end of the path, so the embed points at a GIF that does not exist (or a different one). Every Giphy link that has a slug is affected, which is the format Giphy uses for the links it shows in the address bar and the share menu. Links without a slug (`giphy.com/gifs/<id>`, `giphy.com/embed/<id>`) work.

**What should happen**

The link should become `https://giphy.com/embed/ZK2W0gl0w0vkI`.

**Repro**

```ts
// from packages/element/tests
import { maybeParseEmbedSrc } from "../src/embeddable";

maybeParseEmbedSrc(
  "https://giphy.com/gifs/theoffice-the-office-tv-michael-scott-ZK2W0gl0w0vkI",
);
// "https://giphy.com/embed/theoffice"
// expected "https://giphy.com/embed/ZK2W0gl0w0vkI"

maybeParseEmbedSrc("https://giphy.com/clips/cat-funny-abc123XYZ");
// "https://giphy.com/embed/cat"
```

In the editor: copy a Giphy GIF page URL and paste it on the canvas.

**Root cause**

`RE_GIPHY` in `packages/element/src/embeddable.ts`:

```
/giphy.com\/(?:clips|embed|gifs)\/[a-zA-Z0-9]*?-?([a-zA-Z0-9]+)(?:[^a-zA-Z0-9]|$)/
```

The lazy `[a-zA-Z0-9]*?` matches nothing, `-?` is skipped, and the capture group takes the first slug word because the `-` after it satisfies `[^a-zA-Z0-9]`. The prefix has to consume everything up to the last `-` for the capture to be the id.

body_text: With reference to @dwelle's comment here: https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw/pull/11997#issuecomment-6255528369 I want to make the case for Markdown-backed rich text in Excalidraw, for two reasons: 1. **CLI and LLM friendliness:** Markdown is lightweight, human-readable, and easy for AI agents to generate and manipulate. I think this could be a real advantage as CLI and agent-driven workflows become more common. 2. **Obsidian compatibility:** The Obsidian Excalidraw plugin supports round-tripping text elements into editable Markdown and back. A proprietary rich text format would make this significantly more complicated, while Markdown would fit naturally into the existing workflow. I believe we could achieve the desired formatting capabilities with a limited Markdown + HTML subset, while keeping a simple WYSIWYG editing experience. --- ## Proposal I propose **Markdown-backed text editing in Excalidraw**: one text element, one WYSIWYG editing experience, and Markdown with a small HTML formatting subset as the editable source. The same text element would support ordinary text and inline formatting, whether it stands alone or labels a rectangle, arrow, or sticky note. ## Content model I would reuse the two existing content fields: | Field | Proposed role | | --- | --- | | `originalText` | The unwrapped Markdown source, including supported HTML spans. This is the source of truth. | | `text` | The generated plain-text display representation, with layout-generated line breaks where needed. | For example, with other element properties omitted: ```json { "type": "text", "originalText": "**Important** warning", "text": "Important warning" } ``` The formatting would come from parsing `originalText` into styled text runs used by the editor, text measurement, Canvas renderer, and SVG export. I initially considered storing generated HTML in `text`, but keeping it plain text seems safer for compatibility with existing Excalidraw code. It would also remain useful for search, clipboard, and integrations expecting ordinary text. The editor could use an internal structured model, but saves would serialize back to `originalText` and regenerate the display representation. There would be no need for a third persisted content field or an editor-specific rich text document. Resizing would change the layout, preserving the source and its intentional line breaks. The key implementation challenge is **consistent text measurement and wrapping across mixed styles**. Bold and italic can change glyph widths, so wrapping needs to work with styled runs rather than treating the entire text element as one font. ## Compatibility The existing [text layout code](https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw/blob/d3a9c2a195182bf65b526ccb7a19de96f4bdfdb3/packages/element/src/textElement.ts#L65-L130) wraps `originalText` as plain text, and the [canvas renderer](https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw/blob/d3a9c2a195182bf65b526ccb7a19de96f4bdfdb3/packages/element/src/renderElement.ts#L660-L716) draws `text` as plain characters. I think the existing fields can evolve to support formatting, but this would require a versioned migration and updates to the relevant text consumers. I am currently unsure if old content such as `**not bold**`, ``, or `[label](target)` should remain literal. If yes, then a format/version marker could distinguish legacy plain-text elements from Markdown-backed text. Existing content could be escaped during conversion, preserving its appearance and preventing repeated conversions. Plain-text API inputs should continue to mean literal text, with Markdown input available explicitly. ## Formatting scope I would start with **bold, italic, strikethrough, underline, and foreground color**, retaining one font family and size per element. Markdown already covers most of this. A small allowlist of HTML tags and span styles can cover underline and color: ```md **Bold** and *italic* ~~Strikethrough~~ and underline Colored text ``` For combined formatting, it would be helpful if we could consider that [Obsidian does not render Markdown inside HTML elements](https://help.obsidian.md/html). Using compatible HTML nesting within styled spans would solve this: ```md Important warning ``` The parser and serializer would need to agree on nesting, escaping, and line breaks. CommonMark's soft-line-break behavior also needs attention, since Excalidraw currently preserves explicit text line breaks. The HTML subset should be sanitized, with supported styling clearly defined. ## Extension hooks for specialized integrations I would also love to see a small, instance-scoped extension API around parsing, rendering, and serialization. For example, Obsidian could recognize: ```md [[Project plan|the plan]] ![[Meeting notes#^summary]] ``` An extension could resolve the displayed label or embedded content while preserving the original syntax when the editor saves. This requires more than a rendering callback. The same resolved text needs to participate in measurement, wrapping, canvas rendering, and SVG export. The important principle is that **the source survives editing**. Showing "the plan" should not replace `[[Project plan|the plan]]` in `originalText`. Similarly, an embedded note should remain a reference rather than become an editable copy of its contents. Without the extension, Excalidraw could display the source literally or use a placeholder. The editor should preserve unrecognized tokens when surrounding text is changed. Asynchronous embeds would need sensible limits, cancellation, and an export fallback. ## Editor implementation I would consider using a small rich text engine behind Excalidraw's existing controls. [Lexical](https://lexicaljs.org/docs/packages/lexical) is an interesting option, especially with its [customizable Markdown import/export transformers](https://lexicaljs.org/docs/packages/lexical-markdown). [ProseMirror](https://prosemirror.net/docs/guide/) with a restricted schema is another. Both provide mature selection, undo/redo, clipboard, composition, and accessibility handling. We would still need custom transformers for color spans, source preservation, and integration tokens. A custom editor would give Excalidraw tighter control and potentially reduce dependencies, but selection and caret positioning across differently styled text is a substantial challenge. A transparent textarea overlay becomes especially difficult when bold or italic changes glyph widths. I would compare a minimal engine integration with a focused custom prototype before choosing. Regardless of the editor, I think the important architectural choice is that **Markdown remains the persisted source**, and the editor's internal document model is transient. ## Benefits - **CLI/LLM friendly:** Readable source can be generated, reviewed, and edited without constructing rich text JSON or calculating formatting offsets. - **Obsidian Markdown interoperability:** Existing editable Markdown text-element workflows can evolve naturally to support formatting. - **Portable content:** The stored source remains independent of the chosen editor engine. - **Consistent UX:** Users get rich text formatting directly on the canvas through Excalidraw's existing controls. - **Extensibility:** Specialized integrations can interpret additional Markdown constructs while preserving their original source. ## Acceptance criteria - Existing drawings preserve literal text, whitespace, wrapping, and container behavior after migration. - Markdown/HTML source survives save, reload, and WYSIWYG edits with equivalent formatting. - Opening and saving without edits preserves the original source. - Resizing changes layout without rewriting intentional source line breaks. - Canvas, SVG, and PNG agree with the editor on styling and layout, including rotated text, bound labels, and sticky notes. - Undo/redo, clipboard, Unicode, mobile input, and accessibility remain reliable. - Extension tokens survive editing and remain intact when the corresponding extension is unavailable. --- I think Markdown-backed rich text could be a meaningful long-term advantage for Excalidraw, especially as more users and tools interact with drawings programmatically. I'd be interested in your thoughts, @dwelle, particularly on whether Markdown could serve as the source of truth for the upcoming rich text implementation. Would also love to collaborate on this feature, once you get started on it.

Using compatible HTML nesting within styled spans would solve this: ```md Important warning ``` The parser and serializer would need to agree on nesting, escaping, and line breaks. CommonMark's soft-line-break behavior also needs attention, since Excalidraw currently preserves explicit text line breaks. The HTML subset should be sanitized, with supported styling clearly defined. ## Extension hooks for specialized integrations I would also love to see a small, instance-scoped extension API around parsing, rendering, and serialization. For example, Obsidian could recognize: ```md [[Project plan|the plan]] ![[Meeting notes#^summary]] ``` An extension could resolve the displayed label or embedded content while preserving the original syntax when the editor saves. This requires more than a rendering callback. The same resolved text needs to participate in measurement, wrapping, canvas rendering, and SVG export. The important principle is that **the source survives editing**. Showing "the plan" should not replace `[[Project plan|the plan]]` in `originalText`. Similarly, an embedded note should remain a reference rather than become an editable copy of its contents. Without the extension, Excalidraw could display the source literally or use a placeholder. The editor should preserve unrecognized tokens when surrounding text is changed. Asynchronous embeds would need sensible limits, cancellation, and an export fallback. ## Editor implementation I would consider using a small rich text engine behind Excalidraw's existing controls. [Lexical](https://lexicaljs.org/docs/packages/lexical) is an interesting option, especially with its [customizable Markdown import/export transformers](https://lexicaljs.org/docs/packages/lexical-markdown). [ProseMirror](https://prosemirror.net/docs/guide/) with a restricted schema is another. Both provide mature selection, undo/redo, clipboard, composition, and accessibility handling. We would still need custom transformers for color spans, source preservation, and integration tokens. A custom editor would give Excalidraw tighter control and potentially reduce dependencies, but selection and caret positioning across differently styled text is a substantial challenge. A transparent textarea overlay becomes especially difficult when bold or italic changes glyph widths. I would compare a minimal engine integration with a focused custom prototype before choosing. Regardless of the editor, I think the important architectural choice is that **Markdown remains the persisted source**, and the editor's internal document model is transient. ## Benefits - **CLI/LLM friendly:** Readable source can be generated, reviewed, and edited without constructing rich text JSON or calculating formatting offsets. - **Obsidian Markdown interoperability:** Existing editable Markdown text-element workflows can evolve naturally to support formatting. - **Portable content:** The stored source remains independent of the chosen editor engine. - **Consistent UX:** Users get rich text formatting directly on the canvas through Excalidraw's existing controls. - **Extensibility:** Specialized integrations can interpret additional Markdown constructs while preserving their original source. ## Acceptance criteria - Existing drawings preserve literal text, whitespace, wrapping, and container behavior after migration. - Markdown/HTML source survives save, reload, and WYSIWYG edits with equivalent formatting. - Opening and saving without edits preserves the original source. - Resizing changes layout without rewriting intentional source line breaks. - Canvas, SVG, and PNG agree with the editor on styling and layout, including rotated text, bound labels, and sticky notes. - Undo/redo, clipboard, Unicode, mobile input, and accessibility remain reliable. - Extension tokens survive editing and remain intact when the corresponding extension is unavailable. --- I think Markdown-backed rich text could be a meaningful long-term advantage for Excalidraw, especially as more users and tools interact with drawings programmatically. I'd be interested in your thoughts, @dwelle, particularly on whether Markdown could serve as the source of truth for the upcoming rich text implementation. Would also love to collaborate on this feature, once you get started on it.", "language": "TypeScript", "state": "open", "assignees": [], "locked": false, "verified_at": "2026-10-22T17:41:48.150Z", "expires_at": "2026-10-23T17:41:48.150000+00:00", "timeline_complete": true, "bucket": "historical_signal_only"}

Would extracting the editor's image insertion and cache orchestration into a dedicated module be a useful follow-up to the recent `App.*` refactors, such as #12258?

I'd be interested in implementing this, but would appreciate maintainer feedback on whether the boundary below makes sense before starting.

## Motivation

[`App.tsx`](https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw/blob/6f0a4d19b577e781ee5491d6cb89799b3fba7ee8/packages/excalidraw/components/App.tsx) still coordinates a related group of image responsibilities:

- `insertImages`, `newImagePlaceholder`, and `initializeImage`: placeholders, normalization, file IDs, resizing/size checks, file registration, and insertion.
- `getLatestInitializedImageElement` and `getImageNaturalDimensions`: looking up the latest element across asynchronous work and sizing the inserted image.
- `updateImageCache`, `addNewImagesToImageCache`, and `scheduleImageRefresh`: populating the cache, updating error status, invalidating shape caches, and requesting redraws.

These methods interact with the same files, scene, and image cache, but remain in the main component. Grouping their orchestration could make this workflow easier to follow and test, following the existing `App.*` module pattern. This is a maintainability proposal; I haven't established a performance benefit or a new user-facing bug.

## Proposed boundary

- Introduce an internal module such as `App.images.ts`, following the existing modules' conventions.
- Move the image workflow above, while reusing the existing lower-level image/file utilities and preserving current cache ownership and rendering behavior.
- Keep general drop handling, canvas pointer handling, and toolbar event wiring in `App`; delegate the image-specific work. Preserve existing entry points where callers need them.
- Preserve public APIs, file formats, image options, history behavior, and error handling. No new dependencies are proposed.

## Verification

Run the existing image, clipboard, and drop-related tests, and add focused regression coverage where needed for insertion/dimensions, repeated files, failures, and a placeholder being modified or deleted while initialization is pending. Compare behavior before and after, and manually check toolbar, paste, and drag-and-drop insertion in the browser.

Would this be worth pursuing, and would you prefer insertion and cache orchestration together or a narrower boundary? If work is already planned here, I'm happy to coordinate.

### Steps to reproduce

1. In a spreadsheet, select a range whose top-left cell is empty and whose column headers are numbers, for example years:

   |       | 2023 | 2024 |
   |-------|------|------|
   | North | 10   | 20   |
   | South | 5    | 6    |

2. Copy it and paste it onto the canvas. The pasted text reaches `tryParseSpreadsheet` as:

   ```
   	2023	2024
   North	10	20
   South	5	6
   ```

### Expected

A chart with the series `2023` and `2024` and the labels `North` and `South`.

### Actual

`tryParseSpreadsheet` returns data where the header row becomes a data point with an empty label and the values 2023 and 2024, which dwarf the real values. The series are named `Series 1` and `Series 2`.

I reproduced this with `tryParseSpreadsheet` in a unit test, not in the browser. `tryParseCells` in `packages/excalidraw/charts/charts.parse.ts` treats the first row as a header only when none of its cells parse as numbers, so numeric headers are read as data.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Open [Excalidraw](https://excalidraw.com/).

2. Select the Draw tool from the toolbar (or press the corresponding shortcut key).

3. Open the color palette overlay by pressing the S key.

4. Press the B key to select the red color option from the palette.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/48601f52-479c-4b13-8ba6-679c81c42286

Browser: Google Chrome / Mozilla Firefox (Latest version)

OS: Windows / macOS

Device: Desktop

@Phillip9587 suggested an issue for this in #764. Measured on `master` (`02101da`) with Node 26; the Express results use Express 5.3.0.

`normalizeOptions`, one option at a time:

| option | `42` | `false` | `0` | `''` | `{}` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `inflate` | `true` | `false` | `true` | `true` | `true` |
| `limit` | `42` | throws | `0` | throws | throws |
| `verify` | throws | `false` | `false` | `false` | throws |
| `defaultCharset` | `42` | `'utf-8'` | `'utf-8'` | `'utf-8'` | `{}` |

`type: 42` is accepted, and `shouldParse()` then returns `false` for an `application/json` request, so the parser quietly skips it.

`defaultCharset` across the parsers, for a request without a charset:

| | `'UTF-8'` | `42` or `{}` |
|---|---|---|
| `json()` | 415 `unsupported charset "UTF-8"` | each request throws `TypeError: charset.slice is not a function` (500 in Express) |
| `urlencoded()` | throws at construction | throws at construction |
| `text()` | 200 | throws `TypeError: encoding.toUpperCase is not a function` inside the `raw-body` callback; Express cannot catch it and the process exits |

All three treat `0`, `false` and `''` as `'utf-8'`.

So one option gets three policies: checked at construction in `urlencoded()`, per request in `json()`, and not at all in `text()`, where a non-string value ends the process on the first request.

The question for the next major is which policy all options follow: check types at construction and throw, as `limit` and `verify` partly do, or coerce. Either way, `defaultCharset` needs lower-casing before the `utf-8`/`iso-8859-1` checks, which is what #764 does.

### Summary

All parsers in `body-parser` inflate compressed request bodies by default (`inflate: true`). In 2.x this includes Brotli (`br`). Many users may be unaware that their app decompresses attacker-controlled request bodies.

I'd like to propose making inflation opt-in in the next major version.

### Proposal

- Change the default of `inflate` to `false` (semver-major).
- Document the change prominently in the migration notes.

### Example

With this change, request inflations are opt-out by default and users should knowingly opt in.

```js
app.use(express.json({ inflate: true }))
app.use(express.urlencoded({ extended: false, inflate: true }))
```

### Motivation

**Primary: CVE-2026-111497**

CVE-2026-111497 is an out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder bundled with Node.js that can lead to remote code execution. It is fixed in 22.23.4, 24.22.1 and 26.12.1. An application is exposed when it decompresses attacker-controlled Brotli data, such as a request body.

With the current defaults, any Express 5 app using the built-in body parsers decodes `Content-Encoding: br` request bodies. Patching Node.js is the real fix. Still, an opt-in default would have kept this attack surface closed for the many apps that never need compressed request bodies.

**Secondary considerations**

- WAF bypasses. Some WAFs and proxies do not decompress request bodies. The app silently accepting encodings that the inspection layer may not see is a risk users should opt into knowingly.
- Decompression bombs. `limit` mitigates this. However, CVE-2026-12590 showed that a misconfigured `limit` could silently disable size enforcement, so accepting compressed bodies should be a deliberate choice.

body_text:
The existing res.status implementation correctly accepts the inclusive 100-999 range and rejects out-of-range integers. The regression tests can observe Node's later HTTP validation instead of Express's own synchronous validation.

At 7ef98448f8b38099ab1ded55e458538ad47a51e7, temporarily replacing the range condition in lib/response.js with if (false) leaves the existing HTTP checks for 99 and 1000 passing: Node rejects those values when the response ends, with an error matching the existing expectation.

The test-only correction is to assert directly that Object.create(express.response).status(99) and status(1000) raise RangeError, while keeping the HTTP checks. Direct tests also cover acceptance of 100 and 999, the returned response object, and the stored statusCode. Testing 100 directly avoids interim-response behavior over HTTP.

Reproduction:

1. Run npm run lint and npm run test-ci on the proposed tests: 1,263 tests pass.
2. In an isolated copy, temporarily replace code < 100 || code > 999 in res.status with false.
3. The two direct rejection assertions fail with Missing expected exception (RangeError). Without those direct assertions, the HTTP tests stay green.
4. Restore the condition; all tests pass.

Prepared with AI assistance using [Supertest](https://github.com/renanmpimentel/supertest), a test-effectiveness audit skill. Its concrete benefit here was revealing a validation regression hidden by the HTTP boundary and verifying that the strengthened tests detect it. This report concerns test coverage; application behavior is unchanged.

Environment: Express 5.2.1, Node 24.13.0, Linux.

body_text:
`res.send()` stopped adding `Content-Length` when a `Transfer-Encoding` header is present (#4893, #7459), because the two must not be sent together (RFC 9112 §6.2). `res.redirect()` still sets `Content-Length` unconditionally, so it produces the same invalid response:

```js
app.use((req, res) => {
  res.set('Transfer-Encoding', 'chunked')
  res.redirect('http://google.com')
})
```

Node's HTTP client rejects the response with `Parse Error: Content-Length can't be present with Transfer-Encoding`.

Expected: `res.redirect()` follows the same rule as `res.send()` and omits `Content-Length` when `Transfer-Encoding` is set.

body_text:
Hi! 🙂 `res.send()` with a typed array that is not a `Uint8Array`, for example a `Uint16Array`, gives two different results. The result depends on the `etag` setting and on the length of the array.

## Environment information

**Version**: express 5.3.0

**Platform**: Darwin 27.0.0

**Node.js version**: v24.21.0

**Any other relevant information**: None.

## What steps will reproduce the bug?

```js
const express = require('express')

async function run (etag, length) {
  const app = express()
  app.set('etag', etag)
  app.get('/', (req, res) => res.send(new Uint16Array(length).fill(0x0102)))
  app.use((err, req, res, next) => {
    console.log(String(err))
    next(err)
  })
  const server = app.listen(0)
  await new Promise((resolve) => server.once('listening', resolve))
  const res = await fetch(`http://localhost:${server.address().port}`)
  const body = Buffer.from(await res.arrayBuffer())
  const shown = res.status === 200 ? `${body.length} bytes: ${body.toString('hex').slice(0, 16)}` : ''
  console.log(`etag ${etag}, ${length} elements -> ${res.status} ${shown}`.trimEnd())
  server.close()
}

;(async () => {
  await run(true, 2)
  await run(false, 2)
  await run(false, 1000)
})()
```

Output with `NODE_ENV=test`, which stops Express from logging the error a second time:

```
etag true, 2 elements -> 200 2 bytes: 0202
TypeError [ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE]: The "chunk" argument must be of type string or an instance of Buffer or Uint8Array. Received an instance of Uint16Array
etag false, 2 elements -> 500
etag false, 1000 elements -> 200 1000 bytes: 0202020202020202
```

The second line is the error that the error handler logs.

## What is the expected behavior?

The same behavior with ETag on or off, and for any length. The response is either all the bytes of the array or a clear error.

## What do you see instead?

- With ETag (the default): status 200, but each element is cut to its low byte. Half of the data is lost.
- Without ETag and fewer than 1000 elements: status 500.
- Without ETag and 1000 elements or more: status 200, with the same lost data as with ETag.

## Additional information

`res.send()` accepts any `ArrayBuffer.isView()` value as binary data ([`lib/response.js:151`](https://github.com/expressjs/express/blob/0dee2c52c7c873498f8ed7d8ee4ddd0a04d3ada8/lib/response.js#L151)). Then the value goes one of two ways ([line 170](https://github.com/expressjs/express/blob/0dee2c52c7c873498f8ed7d8ee4ddd0a04d3ada8/lib/response.js#L170)):

- `Buffer.from(chunk, encoding)` ([line 175](https://github.com/expressjs/express/blob/0dee2c52c7c873498f8ed7d8ee4ddd0a04d3ada8/lib/response.js#L175)), when ETag is on or the array has 1000 elements or more. For a typed array, `Buffer.from()` copies the element values, not the bytes.
- Directly to `this.end()` ([line 218](https://github.com/expressjs/express/blob/0dee2c52c7c873498f8ed7d8ee4ddd0a04d3ada8/lib/response.js#L218)), when ETag is off and the array is small. Node only accepts a string, a `Buffer` or a `Uint8Array` there, so it throws.

Support for `Uint8Array` came in 5.1.0 (#6285). Express 4.22.3 sends a typed array as JSON, so this affects 5.1.0 and later.

This came up in other PRs:

- #7433, closed without a merge, was changed to keep the truncated output for compatibility.
- In #7511, @peralva noted the truncation and proposed `Buffer.from(chunk.buffer, chunk.byteOffset, chunk.byteLength)` for every view. The author kept multi-byte typed arrays out of that PR, as a follow-up for the maintainers to decide.
- A review on #7410 noted that its change would make the 500 the default.

This issue is for that follow-up. Sending the bytes of the view, as @peralva proposed, or limiting binary support to `Uint8Array`, changes the response for these arrays. So I did not open a PR. Happy to open one in the direction you prefer 🙌
